set.pl: Farm in sec 17 T31N R19E (Town of Beaver), by the Pelican lakes
pinev: Parcel-level: 1912 Ogle Marinette County atlas shows the family's 120 acres in S-central sec. 17 T31N R19E with a house mark, just NW of the Pelican lakes, about 5 mi W of Beaver village; the 1938 aerial shows the farmstead there (about 250 m).
set.st: In 1924 about $11,200 was stolen from a farmer near Beaver by a relative, who pleaded guilty. About $3,000 was recovered buried on the farm and several thousand more turned up in Minneapolis. In Apr 1925 the thief's lawyers said she confessed that upwards of $5,000 remained buried about 20 feet west of a small birch tree on the farm, some 30 paces to the left of where the recovered $3,000 had been dug up. On the night of 25 Apr 1925 twenty-two men dug by lantern and flashlight under armed guard, joined by the sheriff's men, and found nothing; no later find was reported. Pin is on the 1912 house mark, not the spot itself.
set.t: Caution: the 1924 court record says $6,000 was found buried on the farm and the rest was invested in St. Paul; the 1925 'still buried' claim came via the lawyers. No later recovery reported 1925-40. The birch tree is long gone; the recovered-$3,000 hole would be the reference point, with the claimed cache about 30 paces to its left. Private farmland: permission.

src: Ogle, Standard Atlas of Marinette County, Wisconsin (1912)
